subject: DPA question: staged retention windows and on-demand geo-wipe playbook

Thanks for the draft DPA. Our legal team has a couple of follow-ups specifically around the retention and deletion portions (Annex B) and the operational playbook for on-demand geo-wipes:

- Can you confirm the proposed retention tiers (hot cache / short-term logs / backups) and the default retention windows Redwood is comfortable committing to?

Hi Samir — thanks for the note and the annotated Annex. High-level answers below; I’m attaching our operational checklist (erase-playbook-checklist.pdf) and have looped in Legal (Marissa), and SE (Ben) for any technical/contract language follow-ups.

Staged retention windows (default proposal):
- Hot inference cache: 7 days (mutable, ephemeral)
- Short-term logs / request traces (non-backed): 30 days
- Backups / snapshots (customer-tenanted point-in-time copies): 90 days
- Audit logs / compliance artifacts: 365 days (retention for legal/regulatory reasons; limited access)

Notes: These are our defaults; we can shorten or negotiate windows per account with a clear tiering option in Annex B. Backups are treated separately from ephemeral caches — we do not keep long-lived persistent request data in the hot path.

Geo-wipe / on-demand erase playbook (summary):
1) Receipt & verification: customer submits erase request via Console or signed request to legal@redwood.com; verify account owner and scope.
2) Create internal wipe ticket and freeze cross-region replication for target namespace.
3) Execute primary-region purge (delete objects, purge KV caches, remove pointers).
4) Identify and scrub secondary copies & snapshots; for third-party managed snapshots we trigger delete API calls and log responses.
5) Run verification job that scans object manifests + storage indexes and produces a deletion report.
6) Legal review & certification: Marissa signs the certificate-of-erasure and we deliver a redacted report with object ids and timestamps.
7) Close ticket and archive evidence in a read-only compliance store.

Backups & third-party snapshots: we will call snapshot deletion APIs where available; if a snapshot is immutable/retained by a cloud provider for their own retention, we provide documented evidence of our deletion requests and timeline and continue to work with the provider under the agreed SLAs.

Verification artifact: We can provide a signed certificate-of-erasure + a machine-readable report (CSV) listing object ids, paths, timestamps, and hash fingerpints for deleted manifests. If you need a more rigorous proof-of-wipe (e.g., HSM audit trail), we can add an addendum.

Action items:
- Marissa: suggested contract language / redlines (will follow in-thread).
- Ben/Logan: will provide any technical caveats around immutable snapshots and cross-region replication.

Happy to hop on a 30-min call tomorrow (I’m available 10–11am PT).

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Vanessa — thanks, that helps a lot. A couple of follow-ups after I reviewed:

1) For the 90-day backup window: can you confirm the SLA for deletion of backups after a customer requests a permanent erasure? Acme’s bar for backups is generally 30 days for active deletion requests unless we’ve agreed to longer-term archival.
2) For immutable snapshots (e.g., provider-level immutable snapshot retention): what is Redwood's escalation path and typical timeline to get the provider to permanently delete?
3) The verification report you mentioned — would Redwood be willing to provide an auditable CSV with object hashes and a Redwoods-signed certificate within 10 business days of completion? That would satisfy our compliance team.

Also: do you have a sample DPA clause we can start with for the staged deletion schedule and for temporary cross-border fallback processing during outages?

Samir

From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, logan_wright <logan@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-28T14:22:00Z
Subject: Internal: suggested DPA clause language + fallback residency wording

Vanessa / team — drafting quick suggested language for Samir's ask. Two components: (A) staged deletion schedule and (B) temporary fallback residency for resilience. Below are options we can propose; I kept them concise so Legal (Acme) can accept or counter quickly. I attached a plain-text file with a few alternative phrasings (DPA_clause_suggestions.txt).

(A) Staged deletion schedule (proposed clause):
"Customer Data shall be retained in tiers as follows, subject to the Customer's written configuration: (i) ephemeral inference cache — 7 days; (ii) transaction/request logs — 30 days; (iii) backups and snapshots — 90 days; (iv) audit artifacts — 365 days. Upon Customer's written request for permanent erasure, Redwood will: (a) purge data from the active tiers within five (5) business days; (b) initiate deletion of backups and snapshots and use commercially reasonable efforts to ensure removal within thirty (30) calendar days; (c) provide a signed certificate of erasure and a detailed deletion report listing affected object identifiers and timestamps."

(B) Temporary fallback residency (proposed clause):
"In limited circumstances where operational continuity requires temporary cross-border processing (for example, to failover due to regional infrastructure outage), Redwood may process Customer Data outside the Customer's designated region for a period not to exceed forty-eight (48) hours, provided Redwood: (i) notifies the Customer within four (4) hours of the cross-border processing event where reasonably practicable; (ii) limits the processing to the minimum data and duration required for continuity; and (iii) certifies deletion of any transient copies created as part of the failover within five (5) business days following restoration of primary-region operations."

Comments: 1) keep the backup deletion SLA to 30 days for customer-requested permanent erasure to meet Acme's bar; 2) include the signed certificate + CSV with object hashes as the verification artifact; 3) for immutable provider-level retention, include an explicit sentence committing to documented deletion requests and escalation steps with a timeline (e.g., 10 business days to resolve with the provider) — we should avoid promising we can unilaterally delete third-party immutable snapshots.

If everyone is aligned I'll push these suggested lines to Samir and attach the certificate template and erase-playbook.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
